title: The New Depot
briefing: Optional specialism: project risk. Valtren is building a new pharma depot at Kestrow Park: 18 months, 14 million. At month 4 the project risk log has 9 risks, all 'medium', and contingency is 3%.
The project board asks for an independent risk review.

evidence.title: Project risk log
evidence.body: 9 risks, all medium, none quantified. No owner for 'GDP certification of the new depot'.

evidence.title: Schedule
evidence.body: Pharma clients expect to move volume in month 19. GDP certification takes about 3 months after construction finishes in month 16.

evidence.title: Benchmarks
evidence.body: Comparable cold-store builds overran cost by 12% on average and time by 4 months.

questions.prompt: What is the biggest gap in the project risk log?

options.label: GDP certification has no owner and no slack: construction ends month 16, it takes 3 months, clients arrive month 19
options.feedback: A critical-path risk with zero float.

options.label: Every risk is rated medium, which suggests the ratings were never thought through properly
options.feedback: A symptom; the certification gap is the critical issue.

options.label: Only nine risks for a 14 million build, so the log is clearly incomplete
options.feedback: Number of risks isn't the problem.

questions.prompt: Is 3% contingency adequate against the benchmark?

options.label: No: benchmarks suggest about 12% (around 1.7m), against 0.42m held
Yes: the project is well managed and 3% is typical for a fixed-price build contract
options.feedback: Optimism bias is why benchmarks exist.

options.label: No: hold contingency equal to the full benchmark overrun on both cost and time

questions.prompt: What do you recommend to the project board?

options.label: Name a certification owner, run certification alongside fit-out, raise contingency, and give clients a realistic date
options.feedback: Fixes the critical path and sets honest expectations.

options.label: Keep the plan and press the contractor to finish early, protecting the client date with incentives
options.feedback: Benchmarks say overruns are likely; the client date is at risk.

options.label: Pause the project until the risk log is complete and re-approved

questions.prompt: The project manager feels criticised by the review. How do you handle it?

options.label: Go through the findings with her before the board, credit what works, and agree the actions together
Present the findings to the board as they stand, since the review must stay independent
options.feedback: Surprises the person who must act.

options.label: Present the findings as observations rather than issues, to keep her engaged

lesson: Project risk lives on the critical path. Quantify contingency against benchmarks, give every critical risk an owner, and set honest dates.
